entities.summary:
Orbital resonance is a regular and periodic gravitational influence by two orbiting celestial bodies exerted on each other. This phenomenon has been observed in the orbits of planets, moons, asteroids, and comets throughout the solar system. Orbital resonance played a crucial role in the formation and evolution of the solar system, shaping the paths of celestial bodies and influencing their interactions. The most notable example of orbital resonance is the 3:2 orbital resonance between Jupiter and Io, a moon of Jupiter, which has been extensively studied and remains one of the most fascinating examples of this phenomenon.

The concept of orbital resonance has far-reaching implications for our understanding of celestial mechanics and the behavior of celestial bodies. It has also been crucial in the development of space exploration, as it allows scientists to better understand the complex interactions between celestial bodies and to predict their behavior. By studying orbital resonance, scientists have gained valuable insights into the formation and evolution of the solar system, and have been able to make more accurate predictions about the behavior of celestial bodies.

One of the most striking examples of the impact of orbital resonance is the observation that the orbital periods of the moons of Uranus are in a 4:1 ratio with the orbital period of Uranus itself. This observation has led to a deeper understanding of the complex interactions between celestial bodies and has provided valuable insights into the formation and evolution of the solar system. As one scientist noted, 'Orbital resonance is a subtle but powerful force that shapes the behavior of celestial bodies, and its study has revolutionized our understanding of the solar system.'
